text.p: Tanzanian Finance Minister Simon Mbilinyi has resigned after months of speculation over his role in a damaging imports tax scandal, an official at the presidency in the capital Dar es Salaam said on Monday.
"Up to now, the president has appointed Mr (Daniel) Yona to act as finance minister," said the official. "Mbilinyi has resigned effective immediately."
Mbilinyi's resignation comes on the eve of an international investment forum in Dar es Salaam which aims to promote Tanzania as a stable base in East Africa for foreign investment.
Bitter wrangling had taken place within the ruling CCM party over the past few weeks on whether Mbilinyi should step down on allegations about his role in a tax exemption scandal.

"There were a number of things, including complaints in parliament, about the tax exemptions on imported (edible) oils. It was a very controversial issue and there has been a report on the case which I think did not clear him properly," a senior a central Bank of Tanzania official told Reuters.
Daniel Yona, an economist, is currently minister of state for planning. He formerly worked at the Bank of Tanzania.

A parliament probe report published in September said Mbilinyi acted improperly over imports of cooking oil and should be "taken to task". It added that Mbilinyi ignored advice from his ministry officials who said the oil should not receive any tax exemption.

The exemptions were given to four local companies and covered a shipment of 4,700 tonnes of cooking oil. Importers were allowed to pay import duty at a concessional rate well below the amount stipulated in government statutes.

A similar import tax exemption scandal discovered by the World Bank in 1994 led to the downfall of then finance minister Kighoma Malima and a suspension of $200 million in donor balance of payments support.
